pinacosaurus-hilwitnorum:study:1.title: The morphology and systematics of Pinacosaurus (Historical Biology, 2026)

facts.statement: The type locality for Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum is the Djadochta Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: Djadochta Formation

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum was found in Mongolia.
facts.quote: Country: Mongolia

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum is a newly described species.
facts.quote: Novelty: Sp. nov

facts.statement: Penkalski described the species Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum.
facts.quote: Authors: Penkalski

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum was named by Penkalski in 2026.
facts.quote: subdivision: †Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum Penkalski, 2026

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lived in Mongolia and China during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus (meaning "plank lizard") is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in what is now Mongolia and China during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago).

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaurine about 5 meters long and weighing up to 1.9 metric tons.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaurine, about 5 m long and weighed up to 1.9 MT.

facts.statement: The head of Pinacosaurus was protected by bone tiles, which is the origin of its name meaning "plank lizard".
facts.quote: The head was protected by bone tiles, hence its name.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus used a smooth beak to bite low-growing plants, which were sliced by small teeth and processed in an enormous hind gut.
facts.quote: A smooth beak bit off low-growing plants that were sliced by rows of small teeth and then swallowed to be processed by the enormous hind gut.

facts.statement: The neck, back, and tail of Pinacosaurus were protected by armor made of keeled osteoderms.
facts.quote: Neck, back and tail were protected by an armour of keeled osteoderms.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus could actively defend itself using a tail club.
facts.quote: The animal could also actively defend itself by means of a tail club.

facts.statement: The generic name Pinacosaurus is derived from the Greek word for "plank," referring to the small rectangular scutes on its head.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek πίναξ, pinax, "plank", in reference to the small rectangular scutes covering the head.

facts.statement: The holotype of Pinacosaurus grangeri, AMNH 6523, was found in the Campanian-aged Djadokhta Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, AMNH 6523, was found in a layer of the Djadokhta Formation, dating from the Campanian.

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype is the largest known skull of the genus Pinacosaurus.
facts.quote: The skull is still the largest known of the genus.

facts.statement: Entire bonebeds of juvenile Pinacosaurus have been uncovered at the Alag Teeg site, now part of the Alagteeg Formation.
facts.quote: At another site, Alag Teeg now considered part of the Alagteeg Formation, entire bonebeds have been uncovered of juvenile animals.

facts.statement: Unlike many ankylosaurs preserved on their backs, most Pinacosaurus juveniles are found on their bellies in a resting position with legs tucked in.
facts.quote: Whereas ankylosaur skeletons have often been preserved laying on their back, most Pinacosaurus juveniles are found on their belly in a resting position, with the legs tucked in.

facts.statement: In 2026, Paul Penkalski transferred Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus to the genus Eopinacosaurus based on differences in the skull and cranial osteoderms.
facts.quote: In 2026, Paul Penkalski transferred P. mephistocephalus to its own genus, Eopinacosaurus, based on various differences in the skull and cranial osteoderms.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Heishansaurus pachycephalus is a valid species, as Arbour and Currie concluded in 2015 that it is a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2015, Arbour and Currie again concluded it was a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Robert Hill considered Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus a valid species in 2012 based on secondary dermal horns and narial characteristics, though this status was later challenged.
facts.quote: It was considered a valid species by Robert Hill in 2012, based on the "secondary dermal" (squamosal) horns and narial characteristics.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was a lightly built, medium-sized animal that reached a total length of 5 meters when fully grown.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus was a lightly built, medium-sized animal, fully grown individuals reached a total length of 5 m.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the body mass of Pinacosaurus at 1.9 tonnes, while Thomas R. Holtz estimated it to be similar to that of a horse.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated its body mass at 1.9 t, while Thomas R. Holtz estimated it to have a body mass of a horse.

facts.statement: The upper snout armor of Pinacosaurus consists of a fused mass rather than distinct tiles or caputegulae.
facts.quote: The upper snout armour does not consist of distinct tiles, caputegulae, but of a fused mass.

facts.statement: The known adult skulls of Pinacosaurus have a length of about thirty centimeters.
facts.quote: The adult skulls known have a length of about thirty centimetres.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Pinacosaurus bears about fourteen teeth.
facts.quote: The maxilla bears about fourteen teeth.

facts.statement: The nostril of Pinacosaurus contains at least three smaller oval holes per side within a large narial vestibule.
facts.quote: With Pinacosaurus there are at least three per side.

facts.statement: In juvenile Pinacosaurus, the C hole consists of secondary smaller openings; Godefroit et al. described four pairs in 1999 and a specimen with five pairs in 2003.
facts.quote: In Pinacosaurus juveniles the C hole seems to consist of secondary smaller openings of varying number: Godefroit et al. described four pairs of openings in total in 1999, and in 2003 a juvenile specimen with five pairs of openings was described.

facts.statement: The precise function of the nostril hole arrangement in Pinacosaurus is unclear.
facts.quote: The precise function of this arrangement is unclear.

facts.statement: It was inferred that all dinosaurs had complex tongue bones, but these were generally lost during fossilization.
facts.quote: It was inferred that all dinosaurs had such complex tongue bones but that these were generally lost during fossilisation.

facts.statement: Some bones from the Pinacosaurus juvenile specimen that were initially identified as part of the tongue apparatus were later reinterpreted as the larynx.
facts.quote: However, some of these bones from the specimen were later reinterpreted as the larynx.

facts.statement: Most known postcranial skeletons of Pinacosaurus represent juveniles, and the P. mephistocephalus holotype (IMM 96BM3/1) is no longer than about 3 meters.
facts.quote: Most of these represent juveniles; however, even specimen IMM 96BM3/1, the P. mephistocephalus holotype, is no longer than about 3 m.

facts.statement: The claws of Pinacosaurus are hoof-shaped.
facts.quote: The claws are hoof-shaped.

facts.statement: The foot of Pinacosaurus has three toes, correcting Maryańska's 1977 assumption of four toes which was based on the damaged specimen ZPAL MgD-II/9.
facts.quote: The foot has three toes, not four as Maryańska assumed in 1977, misled by the damaged specimen ZPAL MgD−II/9.

facts.statement: Originally placed in the Nodosauridae by Gilmore, Pinacosaurus is now considered an ankylosaurid and a likely member of the Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Originally placed in the Nodosauridae by Gilmore, Pinacosaurus is now considered to be an ankylosaurid and a likely member of the Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus likely relied on muscular tongues and tongue bones for feeding because its teeth were small and replaced slowly.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus and other ankylosaurs likely relied heavily on muscular tongues and hyobranchia (tongue bones) when feeding, since their teeth were fairly small and were replaced at a relatively slow rate.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Pinacosaurus may have eaten tough leaves and pulpy fruits, though it likely avoided fibrous and woody plants.
facts.quote: Though Pinacosaurus may not have fed on fibrous and woody plants, they may have had a more varied diet, including tough leaves and pulpy fruits.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pinacosaurus exhibited ant-eater-like insectivorous behavior.
facts.quote: Inversely, this might suggest ant-eater-like insectivorous behaviour.

facts.statement: Juvenile Pinacosaurus found at Bayan Mandahu were likely part of a traveling herd killed and buried by a sandstorm.
facts.quote: In the group of juveniles found together at Bayan Mandahu, the individuals were all oriented into the same direction, suggesting they represent a travelling true herd simultaneously killed and covered by a sandstorm.

facts.statement: Later research indicated that the sediments containing Pinacosaurus fossils at Alag Teeg were deposited during a flood, not a drying pool.
facts.quote: The concentration of fossils at Alag Teeg has been explained as caused by a drying pool, but later research showed the sediments were deposited during a flood.

facts.statement: During development, Pinacosaurus juveniles had ribs fused to vertebrae, and their robust forelimbs bore most of the body weight.
facts.quote: During their ontogenetic development, in juveniles at first the ribs fused with their vertebrae. The forelimbs strongly increased in robustness, while the hindlimbs did not become larger relative to the rest of the skeleton, indicating that the arms bore most of the weight.

facts.statement: Yoshida et al. described a fossilized larynx from a juvenile Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum specimen in 2023.
facts.quote: A fossilized larynx was described from a specimen of juvenile P. hilwitnorum (IGM 100/3186) by Yoshida et al. 2023.

facts.statement: The structure of the Pinacosaurus larynx suggests it was capable of making loud, possibly bird-like vocalizations.
facts.quote: This structure suggests that Pinacosaurus was likely capable of making loud, possibly bird-like vocalizations.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus lived in a semi-desert habitat interspersed with oases.
facts.quote: The habitat of Pinacosaurus consisted of a semi-desert interspersed with oases.

facts.statement: It is suggested that Pinacosaurus had a light build to fight small theropods like Velociraptor, using its club to strike swift targets.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that the relatively light build of Pinacosaurus was an adaptation to gain agility to better fight small theropods, the moderately large club being fast enough to hit these swift targets.

facts.statement: The genus Pinacosaurus was named by Gilmore in 1933.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Gilmore, 1933

facts.statement: The first remains of the genus Pinacosaurus were found in 1923, and the type species P. grangeri was named in 1933.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos del género se encontraron en 1923, y la especie tipo Pinacosaurus grangeri fue nombrada en 1933.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was a medium-sized ankylosaur about five meters long and weighing up to two tons.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus era una anquilosaurio de tamaño mediano, de unos cinco metros de largo y que pesaba hasta dos toneladas.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus has between two and five additional openings near the nostrils, the purpose of which remains unexplained.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus tiene entre dos y 5 orificios adicionales junto a las narinas, que todavía no han sido explicados.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Pinacosaurus weight at around 1.9 tons, while Thomas R. Holtz estimated it between 454 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimó su peso alrededor de 1,9 toneladas, sin embargo Thomas R. Holtz lo estimó entre 454 y 907 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus required strong tail muscles to swing its club, with long powerful muscles extending from the hips and legs to support and flex the tail.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus necesitaban unos fuertes músculos en la cola para levantar la maza y blandirla de lado a lado, por lo que unos largos y poderosos músculos se extendían desde las caderas y las patas para sostener la cola y hacerla flexible.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus likely avoided hard stems and pine needles, instead eating soft, low-growing ferns that were easy to cut.
facts.quote: Probablemente evitaban los tallos duros y las agujas de pino y en cambio ingería los blandos y bajos helechos, fáciles de desbrozar.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus had S-shaped nasal passages lined with membranes that likely helped filter and humidify air in desert environments.
facts.quote: En el interior del hocico se presentan multitud de huesos curvos y finos que en conjunto discurren formando una S. Estos conductos nasales se supone que estaban cubiertos por membranas que probablemente ayudaban a respirar mejor en los ambientes desérticos, filtrando y humedeciendo el aire.

facts.statement: Godefroit et al. described four additional nasal openings in 1999, and a juvenile specimen with five openings was described in 2003.
facts.quote: Godefroit et al. describieron cuatro en 1999, y en 2003 un espécimen juvenil fue descrito con cinco aberturas.

facts.statement: The upper snout armor of Pinacosaurus consists of a fused mass rather than distinct scales called caputegulae.
facts.quote: La armadura del hocico superior no consta de baldosas distintas, caputegula, sino de una masa fusionada.

facts.statement: Adult individuals of Pinacosaurus have a skull that is longer than it is wide.
facts.quote: Los individuos adultos tienen un cráneo que es más largo que ancho.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus differs from Crichtonpelta by lacking an ornate posterior edge on the skull roof and having cheek horns that do not curve upward.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus se diferencia de Crichtonpelta en la falta de un borde posterior adornado del techo del cráneo y en que el cuerno de la mejilla no se curva hacia arriba.

facts.statement: Known adult skulls of Pinacosaurus have a length of about 30 centimeters.
facts.quote: Los cráneos adultos conocidos tienen una longitud de unos 30 centímetros.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Pinacosaurus has about 14 teeth.
facts.quote: El maxilar tiene unos 14 dientes.

facts.statement: In Pinacosaurus, nasal opening C is located below opening A, and opening B is on the lower outer side of the vestibule.
facts.quote: En Pinacosaurus, el agujero C está debajo del agujero A y la abertura B está en el lado exterior inferior del vestíbulo.

facts.statement: Godefroit et al. described a total of 4 pairs of nasal openings in 1999, and a juvenile specimen with 5 pairs was described in 2003.
facts.quote: Godefroit et al. describió 4 pares de aberturas en total en 1999, y en 2003 se describió un ejemplar juvenil con 5 pares de aberturas.

facts.statement: The squamosal horn does not cover the entire squamosal bone, creating the illusion of an additional skull bone in front of the horn.
facts.quote: El cuerno escamoso no cubre todo el escamoso, creando la ilusión de que hay un hueso de cráneo adicional frente al cuerno.

facts.statement: A distinguishing feature is that the quadratojugal touches the postorbital, whereas in other Thyreophora where this condition is known, these bones are separated by the jugal.
facts.quote: Un rasgo distintivo real es que el cuadratoyugal toca el postorbital, mientras que en otros Thyreophora para los que se conoce la afección, estos huesos están separados por el yugal.

facts.statement: In 2015, a juvenile specimen was described showing a complex hyoid or tongue bone apparatus.
facts.quote: En 2015, se describió un espécimen juvenil que mostraba un complejo aparato de hueso hioides o de lengua.

facts.statement: Most known postcranial fossils represent juveniles, and even the holotype of P. mephistocephalus, specimen IMM 96BM3/1, does not exceed 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: La mayoría de estos representan juveniles, incluso el espécimen IMM 96BM3/1, el holotipo de P. mephistocephalus, no mide más de 3 metros.

facts.statement: Behind the fused sacral vertebrae are about eight "free" vertebrae, followed by about twenty hardened vertebrae that form the "handle" of the tail club.
facts.quote: Detrás de estas se encuentran unas ocho vértebras "libres", seguidas de unas veinte vértebras endurecidas por proyecciones y que forman el "mango" del garrote de la cola.

facts.statement: The tail club of Pinacosaurus was relatively small compared to other ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Esta porra era relativamente pequeña.

facts.statement: The forelimb has five digits with a phalangeal formula of 2-3-3-3-2, meaning the innermost digit has two bones and the next has three.
facts.quote: Tiene cinco dígitos y la fórmula de la falange es 2-3-3-3-2, lo que significa que el dedo más interno de la extremidad anterior tiene dos huesos, el siguiente tiene tres.

facts.statement: Like all known ankylosaurs, the foot of Pinacosaurus has three toes, not four as Maryańska assumed in 1977 due to damage in specimen ZPAL MgD-II/9.
facts.quote: Como en todos los anquilosáuridos conocidos, el pie tiene tres dedos, no cuatro como supuso Maryańska en 1977, engañado por el espécimen dañado ZPAL MgD-II/9.

facts.statement: The foot phalangeal formula is variable; most individuals have 0-3-3-4-0, some have an additional penultimate phalanx on the third digit resulting in 0-3-4-4-0, while others lack a phalanx on the fourth digit resulting in 0-3-3-3-0.
facts.quote: La fórmula de la falange de los dedos de los pies es variable, la mayoría de los individuos tienen 0−3−3−4−0 pero algunos ejemplares poseen una penúltima falange adicional en el tercer dedo, lo que resulta en 0-3-4-4-0, mientras que otros carecen de una falange en el cuarto dedo del pie, lo que provoca una configuración 0-3-3-3-0.

facts.statement: The neck is protected by two cervical semirings consisting of rectangular segments with keels fused to an underlying bone band.
facts.quote: El cuello está protegido por dos semianillos cervicales, que consisten en segmentos rectangulares con quilla fusionados a una banda ósea subyacente.

facts.statement: While Godefroit assumed Pinacosaurus had three or four neck segments instead of the usual six, Arbour concluded the normal number of segments was present.
facts.quote: Godefroit asumió Pinacosaurus se diferenciaba de otras especies en tener tres o cuatro segmentos en lugar de los seis habituales, pero Arbour concluyó que el número normal estaba presente.

facts.statement: The sides of the flank and tail were occupied by triangular, flat, recurved, and moderately long spines.
facts.quote: Los lados de la rabadilla y la cola estaban ocupados por púas triangulares, planas, recurvadas y moderadamente largas.

facts.statement: On the back were present parallel rows of smaller, keeled, oval osteoderms.
facts.quote: En el dorso estaban presentes filas paralelas de osteodermos de quilla ovalada más pequeños.

facts.statement: There is no continuous "sacral shield" on the hip made of fused plates.
facts.quote: No hay un "escudo sacro" continuo en la cadera, hecho de placas fusionadas.

facts.statement: The precise function of the nasal opening arrangement is unclear.
facts.quote: La función precisa de esta disposición no está clara.

facts.statement: It has been suggested that some additional openings are the result of damage.
facts.quote: también se ha sugerido que algunos orificios adicionales son el resultado de daños.

facts.statement: The higher number of openings in juveniles might be explained by cartilage plates that have not yet ossified.
facts.quote: El mayor número de juveniles podría explicarse por las láminas de cartílago que aún no se han osificado.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus is the best-known ankylosaurid in Asia, with 15 specimens known.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus es el mejor anquilosáurido conocido en Asia con 15 especímenes

facts.statement: The best-preserved skull belongs to a juvenile specimen described by Teresa Maryanska in 1971 and 1977.
facts.quote: El mejor cráneo pertenece a un ejemplar joven descrito por Teresa Maryanska en 1971 y 1977

facts.statement: The holotype, AMNH 6523, consists of a crushed partial skull, jaws, and dermal bone plates discovered in 1923 by Walter Wallis Granger.
facts.quote: El holotipo, AMNH 6523, es un cráneo parcial aplastado, mandíbulas, y placas óseas dermales descubiertas en 1923 encontrados por Walter Wallis Granger

facts.statement: In 1933, Charles Whitney Gilmore described a right ilium and a tail vertebra without yet naming the animal.
facts.quote: En 1933, Charles Whitney Gilmore describió un ilion derecho y una vértebra de la cola, sin nombrar aún al animal

facts.statement: In a later publication that same year, he named and described the type species P. grangeri.
facts.quote: En una publicación posterior del mismo año, nombró y describió la especie tipo P. grangeri

facts.statement: The generic name is derived from the Greek pinax, meaning 'tablet', referring to the small rectangular shields covering the head.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego πίναξ, pinax , "tabla", en referencia a los pequeños escudos rectangulares que cubren la cabeza

facts.statement: The specific name honors Granger, who accompanied the 1923 expedition as a paleontologist.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a Granger, quien acompañó a la expedición de 1923 como paleontólogo

facts.statement: The holotype was found in a layer of the Djadokhta Formation, which dates to the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: El holotipo, AMNH 6523, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Djadokhta, que data del Campaniense

facts.statement: Soviet-Mongolian expeditions in 1969 and 1970 reported finding thirty skeletons.
facts.quote: Las expediciones soviético-mongoles de 1969 y 1970 informaron de treinta esqueletos

facts.statement: Mongolian-Japanese expeditions added another thirty specimens between 1993 and 1998.
facts.quote: Las expediciones mongol-japonesas agregaron otras treinta entre 1993 y 1998

facts.statement: Canadian expeditions reported 40 specimens between 2001 and 2006.
facts.quote: 40 fueron reportadas por expediciones canadienses entre 2001 y 2006

facts.statement: In Bayan Mandahu, Inner Mongolia, the Canada-China Dinosaur Project found specimens in 1987, 1988, and 1990.
facts.quote: En Mongolia Interior en Bayan Mandahu, el Proyecto de Dinosaurios Canadá-China en 1987, 1988 y 1990 encontró especímenes

facts.statement: Undescribed material included two finds of crowded juveniles, evidently killed by a sandstorm.
facts.quote: Otro material, aún no descrito, incluyó dos hallazgos de varios jóvenes apiñados, evidentemente asesinados por una tormenta de arena

facts.statement: While ankylosaur skeletons are often found lying on their backs, most Pinacosaurus juveniles are found lying on their stomachs in a resting position with legs folded inward.
facts.quote: Mientras que los esqueletos de anquilosaurios a menudo se han conservado acostados boca arriba, la mayoría de los juveniles de Pinacosaurus se encuentran boca abajo en una posición de reposo, con las piernas dobladas hacia adentro

facts.statement: In 1952, Maleev named a new ankylosaurid, Syrmosaurus viminicaudus, but it is now considered a junior synonym of P. grangeri.
facts.quote: en 1952 Maleev nombró a un nuevo anquilosáurido, Syrmosaurus viminicaudus, pero actualmente a ambos se los considera como sinónimo más moderno de P. grangeri

facts.statement: Additional remains from Bayan Madahu Formation, Inner Mongolia, China, were described as a new species, P. mephistocephalus, by Godefroit et al. in 1999.
facts.quote: Restos adicionales proveneientes de la Mongolia Interior, China en la Formación Bayan Madahu han sido descritos como una nueva especie P. mephistocephalus por Godefroit et al. en 1999

facts.statement: The specific name is a contraction of Mephistopheles and Greek kephalè, meaning 'head', referring to the 'diabolical' dermal horns.
facts.quote: El nombre específico es una contracción de Mephistopheles y griego κεφαλή, kephalè, "cabeza", en referencia a los cuernos escamosos "diabólicos"

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul suggested that P. mephistopheles was a junior synonym of P. grangeri.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul sugirió que P. mephistopheles era un sinónimo más moderno de P. grangeri

facts.statement: It was considered a valid species by Robert Hill in 2012, based on secondary dermal horns and nasal characteristics.
facts.quote: Fue considerada una especie válida por Robert Hill.en 2012, basado en los cuernos "dérmicos secundarios" (escamosos) y las características nariales

facts.statement: In 2014, Arbour concluded again that Heishansaurus pachycephalus was a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: En 2014, Arbour concluyó nuevamente que era un nomen dubium

facts.statement: In 1995, Eric Buffetaut referred ankylosaurian remains found in Shandong to a Pinacosaurus sp.
facts.quote: En 1995, Eric Buffetaut refirió los restos de anquilosaurios encontrados en Shandong a un Pinacosaurus sp.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus was originally classified in the family Nodosauridae but is now considered a member of Ankylosauridae and likely Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Clasificación Originalmente fue ubicado dentro de la familia Nodosauridae, pero hoy se lo considera perteneciente a Ankylosauridae y un miembro probable de Ankylosaurinae.

facts.statement: Large theropods are not known to have inhabited the Pinacosaurus ecosystem, though smaller ones like Velociraptor were present.
facts.quote: No se sabe que los terópodos grandes hayan habitado el ecosistema , aunque sí estuvieron presentes otros más pequeños como Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Pinacosaurus's relatively light build was an adaptation to gain agility and fight small theropods better.
facts.quote: Se ha sugerido que la construcción relativamente ligera de Pinacosaurus era una adaptación para ganar agilidad y luchar mejor contra pequeños terópodos

facts.statement: In juveniles, the ribs initially fused with their vertebrae during ontogenetic development.
facts.quote: En los juveniles al principio las costillas se fusionaron con sus vértebras.

facts.statement: The front legs became considerably more robust while the hind legs did not grow larger relative to the rest of the skeleton, indicating the arms supported most of the weight.
facts.quote: Las patas delanteras aumentaron considerablemente en robustez, mientras que las patas traseras no se hicieron más grandes en relación con el resto del esqueleto, lo que indica que los brazos soportaron la mayor parte del peso.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus and other ankylosaurs likely relied heavily on muscular tongues and hyobranchial bones for feeding because their teeth were small and replaced slowly.
facts.quote: Pinacosaurus y otros anquilosaurios probablemente dependían en gran medida de las lenguas musculares y los hiobranquios, huesos de la lengua, cuando se alimentaban, ya que sus dientes eran bastante pequeños y se reemplazaban a un ritmo relativamente lento.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pinacosaurus ate fibrous and woody plants, though it may have had a varied diet including tough leaves and fleshy fruits.
facts.quote: Aunque es posible que Pinacosaurus no se haya alimentado de plantas fibrosas y leñosas, es posible que hayan tenido una dieta más variada, que incluye hojas duras y frutas pulposas.

facts.statement: Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum lived from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2

facts.statement: Zhu et al. (2026) described new fossil material of Pinacosaurus grangeri from the Upper Cretaceous Wulansuhai Formation in China and reported possible evidence of sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Zhu et al. (2026) describe new fossil material of Pinacosaurus grangeri from the Upper Cretaceous Wulansuhai Formation (China), refine the diagnosis of this species, study changes in its skull morphology during its life history, and report possible evidence of sexual dimorphism.

rejected.statement: The body of Pinacosaurus was flat and low-slung, though not as heavily built as in some other ankylosaurines.
rejected.quote: Its body was flat and low-slung but not as heavily built as in some other members of the Ankylosaurinae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'not as heavily built as in some other'

rejected.statement: Each nostril of Pinacosaurus was a large depression pierced by between three and five smaller holes, the function of which is uncertain.
rejected.quote: Each nostril was formed as a large depression pierced by between three and five smaller holes, the purpose of which is uncertain.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a large depression pierced by between three and'

rejected.statement: The holotype consists of a partially crushed skull, lower jaws, the first two neck vertebrae, and dermal bones collected in 1923.
